name: Singaporean xinyao (Mandarin youth folk)
lineage: Singaporean xinyao ("Singapore songs") Mandarin-language singer-songwriter youth-folk movement emerging in early-1980s Singapore among ethnic-Chinese tertiary-education students at the National University of Singapore, Nanyang Technological Institute, and the major junior colleges. The form developed as a youth-cultural alternative to Cantopop and Mandopop commercial-pop dominance, with simple acoustic-guitar-accompanied original Mandarin-language compositions addressing youth concerns, campus life, and Singaporean identity. The Liang Wern Fook ensemble and Singapore Youth Festival 1983-1985 xinyao competitions consolidated institutional visibility. Distinguished from Taiwan campus-folk min-ge yundong (1970s) by Singaporean specific cultural-context and Singlish-inflected Mandarin register.
